hook.line: Two apologies sound alike but go to different places: one is sympathy for what happened to someone, the other is owning your own mistake.

examples.en: I'm sorry you were late. (to a friend)
I'm sorry you're sad. (to a friend)
I'm sorry I shouted at you.

rule:
Two apologies, and the difference is who did it.

Someone else, or something that happened to them: *Siento que* + a changed ending. *Siento que hayas llegado tarde.* *Siento que estés triste.*

You did it yourself: *Siento haber* + the *-ado/-ido* word, with no *que*. *Siento haber llegado tarde.* For *didn't*, add *no*: *Siento no haber llamado.*

The common slip is using *que* for your own action. If the sorry is about *you*, think *haber*.
smallPrint: Teachers call this the subjunctive after *siento que* when the subjects differ, and the perfect infinitive when they are the same.

options: I'm sorry you shouted at me.
I'm sorry I shouted at you.

readAndPick.es: Siento que Vale se haya ido.
Siento que te hayan dicho eso.
options: I'm sorry I said that to you.
I'm sorry they said that to you.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *haber llegado* or *que llegué*, then type the whole sentence: Siento ___ tarde. (I'm sorry I was late.)
yourTurn.why: You did it yourself, so *haber* and no *que*.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *que estés* or *estar*, then type the whole sentence: Siento ___ triste. (I'm sorry you're sad. To a friend.)
yourTurn.why: It's about the other person, so *que* and *estés*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: I'm sorry you can't come. (to a friend)
Type it in Spanish: I'm sorry I didn't call.
Type it in Spanish: I'm sorry Hernando is ill.
yourTurn.why: Hernando is someone else, so *que* and *esté*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say it about yourself: *Siento que hayas llegado tarde.* becomes: I'm sorry I was late.
yourTurn.why: Now you did it, so *haber* replaces *que*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: I'm sorry I forgot your birthday. (to a friend)

pitfalls.why: Almost. When *you* did it, drop *que* and use *haber* plus the *-ado* word.
Almost. After *siento que*, the verb takes the changed ending: *estés*.

pitfalls.right: Siento que Vale se haya ido.
pitfalls.why: Almost. When someone else did it, go back to *que* and the changed ending.

personal: Tell me one thing you're sorry about that you did, and one thing you're sorry about that happened to someone you know. Use *Siento haber...* and *Siento que...*.
